proof.criterion: The review's blocking authz finding: a cookie server with no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* setting must not go on honouring the dsession cookies its sign-in already issued.
proof.surface: The real envoy-dispatch binary built from this head, as a process on a real Postgres (Debian PostgreSQL 17.11 with pgvector at 127.0.0.1:5433), against a database carrying the people and user_sessions rows a sign-in leaves behind, driven over HTTP with curl. That database state is what a converted stack holds and is what makes the request reach the cookie check at all.
proof.command: Minted a dsession cookie for someone@example.com with the deployment's own DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY (auth.IssueSessionCookie through a throwaway cmd/zzmintcookie, deleted after the run), inserted the rows a sign-in leaves (insert into people (email) …; insert into user_sessions (login) …, then select login, generation from user_sessions → someone@example.com|0), started the binary with DATABASE_URL, DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN, DISPATCH_SIGNING_KEY, DISPATCH_LISTEN_HOST, DISPATCH_PORT and DISPATCH_SERVER_URL and no DISPATCH_SIGNIN_* at all, then curl -si -H 'Cookie: dsession=<value>' http://127.0.0.1:18769/api/v1/whoami with no bearer.

trickyParts: The guard reads boot.SignInIssuer, not the signIn argument. Keying it on signIn == nil looked more direct and broke six cases of TestEverySettingReachesItsReader: settings_test.go's appContextFor passes built.SignIn, which a case leaves nil to mean 'cookie identity with no membership check', and reading that nil as 'this deployment configured no sign-in' gave those cases an identity main would never build. signInFlow builds a flow for exactly the boot whose issuer is set, so in every process main starts the two are the same fact.

Handing the harness signInFlow(boot) instead does not work either: with a flow in hand requestIdentityFor builds a Membership, and the cases that wire no people store then dereference a nil pool (store.Pool.QueryRow, SIGSEGV), while giving them a store makes Membership.Confirm end the session of a person no cookie ever recorded. That is why the harness keeps its nil flow.

The refusal is an explicit identity rather than a nil Sessions field. Leaving Sessions nil also returns ErrNoIdentity today, but nothing in CookieIdentity says that is a decision, and a later change to Login would reopen it in silence.

Membership's 'nil only on the local dev sign-in server' is true again after the fix, since no cookie server without sign-in gets a CookieIdentity at all; the comment gained the clause saying where that case went instead of being rewritten.

The cluster-only refusal table's row order moved when it became slices.Concat of the two group tables and the rest. Nothing depends on it: TestDispatchClusterOnlyRefusesEveryDispatchInput sets one input per row, and TestDispatchEveryInputIsLiveOrRefusedUnderClusterOnly sorts before it compares.
deviations: The reviewer suggested expressing the cookie refusal by leaving Sessions nil. It is an explicit identity.NoBrowserIdentity instead, for the reason in trickyParts; the behaviour the reviewer asked for is unchanged.
The reviewer asked for identity.go:34-35 to be corrected. The fix makes that sentence true again, so it is kept and extended rather than rewritten; the thread reply says so.

TestDispatchPartialTailnetGroupNamesEveryMissingInput keeps its name although it now covers both groups and four malformed-value rows: this issue's plan names it and the proof table selects it with -run. The reviewer's naming nit was recorded as skipped in the previous round for the same reason.

Every code commit of this round was already pushed, so nothing was lost; the rootless Postgres harness in $TMPDIR was, which is why the two Postgres-backed rows above quote the runs made at this same head before the recreation rather than being re-run after it.
